title: Cloud Factory
description: Schedule- and event-driven agent orchestration on Cloudflare, per docs/design/cloud-factory.md. Goal: a self-deployed, headless software factory — signals (local agents, Telegram, GitHub issues/CI/PRs, webhooks, cron) become ticks, a deterministic dispatcher ignites runs, orchestrator and worker agents run in Cloudflare Sandboxes under a durable Workflow control plane, and humans stay in the loop only through gates on the operator channel. Git and .tick/ remain the source of truth; the factory is additive — fully local operation stays untouched.
notes:
2026-08-24 22:58 - PROJECT ACCEPTANCE, assessed by Phase 4's closeout (2026-08-24). All four phases are closed; this is where the project's own A1-A6 stand.

  A1 an epic completes with the operator's laptop offline from submission onward
     PARTIAL. Cloud runs dispatch, fan out, collect and merge without a local orchestrator —
     proven repeatedly in Phase 2. What has never been proven is a FULL epic completing that
     way: every evidence run was stopped by me, by a budget, or by a defect. Nothing known
     blocks it; nobody has watched one finish.

  A2 each signal source produces exactly one tick, dedup by external ref, trace ID to the PR
     MOSTLY MET. GitHub issues and webhooks verified live with dedup (Phase 3). Telegram is
     built and deployed but never exercised by a real operator message. Cron sweeps built,
     never fired. The trace id joins signal -> run -> worker logs (hyi).

  A3 budgets enforced from AI Gateway ground truth; a budget stop still runs review and closeout
     MET on enforcement, PARTIAL on the clean stop. Phase 2's 7zk found a budget trip destroying
     three working containers and keeping nothing; the grace window now lets a cancelled worker
     push before it is destroyed, but that path has not been exercised live.

  A4 a local orchestrator drives cloud workers through tk cloud, sharing one lease
     MET. The verb family exists and Phase 2's 7n7 fixed the lease that made wave 2 impossible.

  A5 tk factory trace joins one run's story across all layers
     MOSTLY MET. tk cloud logs (per-tick), trace (gateway), supervisor (liveness) and hyi's
     trace id cover it. The named single command 'tk factory trace' does not exist as such.

  A6 a project never enrolled behaves exactly as before — offline, no daemon
     MET and structurally so: enrolment gates every path, and the local herdr substrate that
     built Phases 3 and 4 never touched the factory.

THE HONEST SUMMARY: the factory works and has been verified live at every layer, but no single
run has yet gone end to end — signal to merged PR — without a human intervening somewhere. That
is A1, and it is the one thing worth doing next. It needs no new capability, only a run nobody
stops.
acceptance_criteria: [A1] An epic submitted with tk cloud run completes — waves, gates, merged PR — with the operator's laptop offline from submission onward. [A2] Each signal source (Telegram message, GitHub issue label, CI failure on a factory PR, PR opened, registered webhook, cron sweep) produces or annotates exactly one tick, with dedup by external ref and a trace ID that follows the work to the PR. [A3] Run budgets are enforced from AI Gateway ground truth, not agent self-report; a budget stop is a clean stop that still runs review and closeout on completed work. [A4] A local orchestrator can drive cloud worker sandboxes through the tk cloud verb family, sharing the same lease as cloud-initiated runs. [A5] tk factory trace joins one run's story across signal, dispatch, workflow, harness log, gateway spend, and tracker layers. [A6] A project never enrolled in the factory behaves exactly as before — offline, no daemon, no cloud dependency.
